I am an old woman, 67 years, and I have farmed this land my whole life here in Mtwara. We do not buy the chemical fertilizers — they are too costly and the shops are far, and our sandy soil here near the coast does not hold them well anyway. I plant the maize seed I saved from last harvest, together with my cassava between the rows like my mother taught me, and I rely on the rains. My grandchildren help me weed and harvest, and when the work is heavy I ask a neighbor's son to help for a few days in exchange for some of the harvest.
